reflections.title: Building a Life on God's Wisdom

reflect.text: Building a stable life and home takes far more than quick, surface fixes. When we lack understanding, our homes can easily become battlefields rather than safe shelters. True wisdom begins with knowing God personally and applying His truth to daily life. When we let Scripture guide our choices, God protects our households from self-destruction and fills our lives with lasting peace.

God's wisdom also changes how we treat the people around us. As F. B. Meyer reminds us, Christ showed that "it was wrong not to do right." It is not enough simply to avoid causing trouble. God calls us to step in and rescue those who are hurting and facing danger. We cannot close our eyes and pretend it is not our business, because God searches our hearts and knows when we fail to show love.

Walking in wisdom does not mean we will never stumble. We might take a wrong turn or fall into sin, but God treats us with great patience. Instead of discarding us, He gently steers us back onto His path. Because our failures are never final in His hands, God's grace gives us the strength to get back up every time we fall.

questions: Where in your home or relationships do you need God's wisdom instead of a quick fix?
Is there someone in trouble whom God is calling you to help rather than ignore?
reflections.prayer: Lord, give us Your wisdom to build our lives on Your truth so our homes may be places of peace. Keep us from turning away when we see others in distress, and teach us to do what is right. Thank You for Your patient grace that lifts us up whenever we stumble. Amen.
